description: Single-panel scatter plot of specific energy absorption versus aluminium content. The y-axis is labelled "Specific energy absorption (J/mm³)" and runs 0.0 to 0.6 in 0.1 steps; break symbols (//) are drawn in the lower-left near the 0.0 level and at the top of the frame. The x-axis is "Al content (wt%)" with printed ticks 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and a further break mark near its left end. All data markers are open diamonds, grouped in near-vertical clusters at approximately 6.5, 7.5, 8.5, 9.5, 10.5, 11 and 11.5 wt% Al. The two markers near 6.5 wt% Al are the lowest, lying between the 0.2 and 0.35 gridlines; every other diamond lies above 0.4 J/mm³, and the single highest marker, near 11 wt% Al, lies between the 0.5 and 0.6 gridlines. In-panel text "Fe-Mn-Al-C steels" labels the diamond series, while "Deformation rate 10³/s" (left) and "Deformation rate 10⁴/s" (right) annotate the loading conditions. Three open squares at low Al content, between the 0.1 and 0.3 gridlines and clearly below every diamond, are arrowed to the labels "IF steel", "HC300LA" and "DC04". The figure therefore demonstrates that Fe-Mn-Al-C steels with Al above roughly 7 wt% absorb about twice the specific energy of conventional deep-drawing steels.

subfigures.description: Scatter plot of specific energy absorption (J/mm³, y-axis 0.0-0.6 with break marks) against Al content (wt%, x-axis ticks 6-12). Open-diamond data points cluster between ~6.5 and ~11.5 wt% Al, mostly above 0.4 J/mm³, highest marker near 11 wt% Al between the 0.5 and 0.6 gridlines. Three open squares representing conventional steels are arrowed to the labels 'IF steel', 'HC300LA' and 'DC04' at low Al content and low absorption (between the 0.1 and 0.3 gridlines). Annotations read 'Fe-Mn-Al-C steels', 'Deformation rate 10³/s' and 'Deformation rate 10⁴/s'.

observations.observation: The figure is a single scatter plot with 'Specific energy absorption (J/mm³)' on the y-axis (ticks 0.0 to 0.6 in 0.1 steps) and 'Al content (wt%)' on the x-axis (printed ticks 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12).
All Fe-Mn-Al-C data points are open diamond markers, arranged in near-vertical clusters at about 6.5, 7.5, 8.5, 9.5, 10.5, 11 and 11.5 wt% Al.
The two diamonds near 6.5 wt% Al are the lowest data points, falling between the 0.2 and 0.35 y-gridlines; all remaining diamonds lie above the 0.4 gridline.
The single highest diamond marker lies near 11 wt% Al, between the 0.5 and 0.6 J/mm³ gridlines.
Three open square markers at low Al content, positioned between the 0.1 and 0.3 J/mm³ gridlines and below every diamond, are arrowed to the labels 'IF steel', 'HC300LA' and 'DC04'.
In-panel text labels the diamond data series as 'Fe-Mn-Al-C steels'.
Two in-panel annotations read 'Deformation rate 10³/s' (left side) and 'Deformation rate 10⁴/s' (right side).
Break symbols (//) are drawn on the y-axis at the lower-left near the 0.0 level and at the top of the frame, and on the x-axis near its left end.

The caption states that the plotted values are specific energy absorption of Fe-Mn-Al-C steels compared with different conventional deep-drawing steels at the crash-relevant strain rate of 10³/s, citing references [6,9].

The caption's stated strain rate (10³/s) covers only one of the two deformation rates annotated in the panel, which also carries a 'Deformation rate 10⁴/s' label; the two rates are not visibly separated by distinct marker symbols at this resolution.
The citing text states the specific energy absorption value of Fe-Mn-Al-C steels is about 0.5 J/mm³ when the Al content is higher than 7%, similar to Mn TWIP steels.

The citing text states conventional deep drawing steels (DC04, HC300LA, high strength IF steels) have specific energy absorption between 0.16 and 0.25 J/mm³, so the Fe-Mn-Al-C value is about fifty percent higher.
The citing text attributes the enhanced energy absorption of Fe-Mn-Al-C steels to severe shear band (adiabatic shear band) formation at high strain rates.

The citing text reports that the Fe-28Mn-12Al-1C alloy in the aged condition [6] shows compressive true strengths greater than 1.5 GPa and true fracture strains exceeding 40% at strain rates between 10³/s and 10⁴/s.

unreadable_items: Exact numerical values of the three conventional-steel square markers are not printed; only their approximate position between the 0.1 and 0.3 J/mm³ gridlines can be read
Marker shape/size does not legibly distinguish the 'Deformation rate 10³/s' from the 'Deformation rate 10⁴/s' diamond data sets, so individual points cannot be assigned to a rate
The exact y-value of individual diamonds can only be read against gridlines, not as printed numbers
